html:
The Yarluyandi, also known as the Jeljendi, are an Aboriginal Australian people of the far northeast of South Australia and the edge of Queensland, on the lower Diamantina River near today's Birdsville.

Their neighbours were the Mithaka to the north, the Ngameni downriver, and the Karangura and Wanggamala. The country is gibber plain and dune, cut by the channels of the Diamantina, which fill only after rain far upstream. Cattle stations and the stock route to the south came in the 1870s and 1880s.
